Elon Musk on why he started Tesla and SpaceX.

"Anyone who starts a car company thinking it's the easy way to make money is a fool. There are only two car companies that have not gone bankrupt in the history of the United States, and that's Ford and Tesla."

He is not selling a lifestyle brand. He is describing two bets he thought would almost certainly fail — and he took them anyway.

• Tesla — within inches of bankruptcy, multiple times
• SpaceX — same cliff, same decade
• His own odds going in: less than 10% chance of success

Most founders optimize for exit math.
He optimized for missions that almost nobody believed could work.

"For both of those companies, I thought I had less than a 10% chance of success, and I thought it was overwhelmingly likely that I would lose the money that I made from PayPal."

Fresh upload attached (~33s) — don’t QT ElonClipsX.

Why Factory

THE CAR ISN'T THE
HARD PART.
THE FACTORY IS.

Most people still treat factories as a cost center.

That's the wrong model.

@elonmusk:

"I love factories. Honestly. A lot of people these days don't love factories or haven't even been to one, but I've walked the line in every factory and I'm a big fan."

"This is a great place to be. You make things that have good utility. People love the product. Building a product people love, that's great."

That's why the factory matters.

• N cost centers — plants treated as overhead
• 1 factory-as-product — designed like the car
• Walk the line — utility people love
• Software scales on servers — hardware scales on a line

The car isn't the hard part.
The machine that makes the machine is.

.@elonmusk on why Starship is hard.

"Starship is the most complicated machine ever made by humans, by a long shot. Any project I can think of would be easier than this, and that's why no one has made a fully reusable orbital rocket."

Most people treat rockets like airplanes with bigger tanks. Elon is saying full reuse is a different class of problem — heat shield, engines that fly twice, tanker rendezvous, and a vehicle that has to work as a system, not a one-shot firework.

• Expendable rockets — throw away the machine every flight
• Partial reuse — booster returns; upper stage still dies
• Full reuse — same ship flies again; cost collapses toward airline economics

Hard is the point.
Reuse is the unlock.
Starship is the vehicle.

"It's a very hard problem that many smart people have failed at."
